tasks.title: Retain explicit task work text and initial review intent safely
tasks.outcome: Read the authoritative TinySpec and the shared worker brief in docs/plans/workflow-monitor-planned-calls-tasks.md#shared-worker-brief. Deliver the retained descriptor contract for new recordings only: full task outcome/description and explicit initial independent-review plan intent, through normalization and closed public readback. Generic review phase vocabulary is not intent. Retain only the explicit work description, not the rest of the task object, prompts, answers or arbitrary payloads. Keep missing evidence within supported new recordings honestly unknown and optional recording nonfatal; never reconstruct text from summaries/current files or impose an invented full-text cap. No old-run support, legacy fallback or compatibility-specific check is required. Leave existing stored history untouched: no deletion, migration or backfill. Do not build a new version/admission framework or systematically preserve/delete legacy support. Adapt the owned descriptor/readback/HTTP fixtures to the supported new contract while retaining genuine privacy, malformed/missing-evidence, pagination and security assertions. Update the affected new-contract descriptor/privacy behavior in workflow_monitor/README.md. Exclude dispatch reconciliation and graph rendering. Prove the real descriptor → Store → Reader → normalize → public boundary with permanent small isolated fixtures before consumers rely on the new facts.

tasks.title: Expose exact scheduled calls and round-only notices before observations
tasks.outcome: Read the source and shared worker brief, then consume T001's retained intent/text contract. Preserve safe review dispatch/attempt facts and exact worker/fixer invocation history through Reader, normalization, closed DTOs and full-snapshot app qualification, including dispatch without observation. A review execution/ordinal identifies a reviewer; a fixing round is NOT an individual call. Expose a typed round-only notice for Details/history, and individual fixing calls only on exact invocation evidence. Preserve every distinct attempt, rejected review and correction lineage within supported new recordings; leave existing stored history untouched. Adapt the owned readback/presentation/history fixtures to the new contract as needed, including test_lineage.py's hard-coded old descriptor and test_observation.py's worker fixture facts; retain genuine lineage, missing-evidence, read-only/security and metric/evidence assertions rather than old-descriptor fallbacks. Reuse app.py _execution_details/_task_progress before paging for qualified execution and task state; do not recalculate authority from a history page or checkpoint status. Use permanent actual producer/store/readback tests to establish available initial worker-root/kind/chain and reviewer identity evidence before T003 reliance. Do not add producer fields speculatively: only a demonstrated necessary exact binding fact with reason; material contract changes return for affected approval. Update readback/dispatch documentation. Exclude graph and UI work, new metrics arithmetic, migrations and writer imports into the monitor.

tasks.title: Reconcile planned slots with exact calls in the production graph projection
tasks.outcome: Read the source/shared worker brief and consume verified T001/T002 contracts and binding proof. Extend actual graphFor/types, not the graph engine: one persistent planned slot per known task worker and explicit initial final-review intent, with later plans retained through execution. Bind a task slot only to a unique evidenced same-run/task initial worker root by kind/chain, never time/label/task-only matching; corrective/retry/other roots remain separate, and ambiguous roots stay distinctly qualified unknown. Bind initial review intent only to unique ordinal 1 plus exact execution ID, then follow that identity. Preserve stable rendered slot identity across status polls. Add exact corrective calls/reviews dynamically, not round endpoints or predicted calls. Give every task-associated node source designation or stable source-order Task N, readable title/role and understandable repeated-call numbering. Distinguish declared dependencies (including planned review completion dependencies) from recorded causal/checkpoint-input links; reject missing/ambiguous/cyclic relations with ordinary qualifications. Keep measured flat ELK DOWN contract. Update projection documentation and permanent production-import graph tests; rendering and Details are downstream.

required.pass_condition: Production graphFor tests compare pre-start/running/returned/failed snapshots: all known plans visible, later calls retained, selected slot ID stable and no duplicate. Resumes/exact chains, dispatch-before-observation, repeated roots, arbitrary task IDs, cross-run/task collisions and conflicting initial-review identities prove only unique exact reconciliation. Ambiguity retains distinct actual calls with unknown reconciliation. Missing proof is not released as working.
required.evidence: Permanent test_graph.spec.ts imports production graphFor and asserts node IDs/counts/lifecycle and matching; consumes T002 boundary evidence rather than manufacturing unavailable facts.
required.permission: Prepared locked web dependencies required. No install/link/bootstrap, no runtime model launch.

required.pass_condition: Rejection→round notice→multiple exact fixing prompts→recorded rereview preserves all nodes/attempts, no guessed endpoints. Declared versus recorded edges have different semantic classification. Labels include useful task designation/title/role and Fix 1/Review 2 distinctions, never opaque IDs/raw enums. Review successful return remains separate from verdict. Existing measured DOWN production layout test stays valid, with no groups/new engine.
required.evidence: Graph tests assert edge semantics, ambiguous/missing/cyclic qualifications, source-order numbering and forbidden label content, plus build/type output.
required.permission: Execution return is not acceptance; only tested helper behavior releases downstream reliance.
